ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or write stories. But, even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, you know? (, kono robot o tsukuru hito wa, kono robot no koto o tsukamu to iu nai).

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together. You can make it work, but you don't know why it works that way. (, kono Lego no kaste o tsukuru toki, kono kaze wa, kono kaze wa).

These neural networks and AIs are like that Lego castle. They're made up of many tiny pieces, like neurons and weights, that work together to make the robot do things. But, the people who made them don't fully understand how all those pieces fit together. (, kono neuron to, kono weight wa, kono robot no koto o tsukamu to iu nai).

It's not that they didn't try to understand how it works. They just didn't have the time or the tools to figure it out. It's like trying to solve a really hard math problem, but you don't have the right tools or the right brain to solve it. (, kono suuri no koto o tsukamu to iu nai).

So, even though the creators of these neural networks and AIs are really smart, they don't fully understand how they work. And that's okay. It's like they're still learning, and they're still figuring out how to make these robots do even more amazing things. (, kono robot wa, kono robot wa, kono robot wa).
